context.summary: Extended ELIXIR-DEV's 16 existing smoke tests (which already cover AC1-AC3 and AC4/AC5's happy path adequately -- verified, not duplicated) with 7 new tests in test/letflow/simulation/runner_template_and_outcomes_test.exs closing real gaps: (1) substring-form {{produces.X}} substitution verified against real Postgres state (not a hardcoded expectation, since the substituted value is a runtime UUID); (2) an unresolved-produces-reference fail-closed test; (3) the design's specifically-named case of a later step referencing a via:gui step's nonexistent produces output, failing closed with :unresolved_template rather than nil/literal-string substitution; (4)/(5) task_assigned and audit_event verification-method match/mismatch test pairs (both had zero prior coverage) proving neither is a 'no error raised' stub. Total simulation-harness test count: 23 passed (16 pre-existing + 7 new), mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean.

findings_for_orch.description: Unlike :task_assigned and :instance_state, the :audit_event verification clause discards its produces argument (bound as _produces) and never runs args through resolve_ref/3's {{produces.X}} template substitution. A scenario cannot write "resource_id" => "{{produces.instance.instance_id}}" in an audit_event expected outcome -- the literal template string is sent to Audit.list_entries/1 verbatim and silently matches nothing (outcome: :fail, not an error). Discovered while writing this session's audit_event test pair; those tests were written to scope by resource_type/event_type only to avoid depending on the broken path. Not fixed here (test/support/simulation/runner.ex implementation is ELIXIR-DEV's file, outside TEST-DESIGNER's remit). Likely to matter concretely for REQ-206/207/208, which own the real scenario corpus and will want resource-id-scoped audit_event checks.
findings_for_orch.recommendation: Route a small fix to ELIXIR-DEV before or alongside REQ-206: have the :audit_event clause call resolve_ref/3 on resource_id (and resource_type, for consistency) before querying, same as the other two methods already do.

findings_for_orch.description: AC3's belt-and-suspenders TOCTOU conflict-branch fallback (retry_onboarding_lookup/2, refetch_user_or_error/2, refetch_group_or_error/2, refetch_process_or_error/2) is not exercised by any test, including this session's additions -- only the pre-check path is. Reasoning recorded in test/specs/REQ-205.md's AC3 section: no injectable seam exists to force the race deterministically without a timing-dependent Task.async test, which this session's own instructions rule out (no wall-clock/unseeded-randomness dependence). Coverage substitute: code-review-level confirmation this session that each fallback branch is reachable and correctly shaped (re-fetches and returns the winner rather than propagating the error).
